etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English touten (“to jut out, protrude, gaze upon, observe, peer”), from Old English *tūtian (“to be sticking out, protrude”), related to Old English tȳtan (“to stand out, be conspicuous, shine”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tut(t)- (“to stick out, project”). Compare Icelandic túta (“a teat-like prominence”), tútna (“to be blown up”). Possibly influenced by dialectal toot (“to stick out; project; peer out; peep”), from Middle English toten, totien, from Old English tōtian (“to peep out; look; pry; spectate”). Compare also Old English tot, ġetot (“pomp, splendour, vainglory”).
senses: Someone advertising for customers in an aggressive way.
A person at a racecourse who offers supposedly inside information on which horse is likely to win.
(transitive) To flaunt, to publicize/publicise; to boast or brag about; to promote.
(UK, slang, horse-racing, transitive) To spy out information about (a horse, a racing stable, etc.).

senses: (card games) In the game of solo, a proposal to win all eight tricks.
